questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before entering the reduced speed zone.
You should slow to 35 mph only when the weather is bad.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell you to slow down. The new speed limit shown on the sign begins right at that sign.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving up or down?

options.text: Yes, if a train is not close.
Yes, if your vehicle will not damage the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: What happens to your field of vision when you drive faster?

options.text: You can see cross traffic more easily.

questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As speed increases and vision decreases, you must watch more carefully for hazards.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on blind curves if no sign is posted?
questions.explanation: The default speed limit on blind curves is 20 mph. If a sign shows a different speed limit, follow the posted sign.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lane and a bicycle is ahead of you. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass while leaving enough space between you and the bicycle.
Keep driving straight. The bicycle rider must get out of your way.
Wait until you reach a traffic light or stop sign before passing.
Honk at the bicycle rider to warn them you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass while leaving enough space between you and the bicycle.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicycle the same way you pass any vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on regular roads, or 5 feet on faster roads or when passing multiple bicycles. Do not honk suddenly, as it may startle riders and cause a crash.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Open your door to see behind you.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol reduce the alcohol in your blood?
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. While it may help you stay awake, it cannot change how much alcohol is in your blood or make you sober.

questions.question: At dusk or on cloudy days, what should you do with your lights?

options.text: Do not turn on any lights.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on cloudy days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of oncoming traffic or within 500 feet of the vehicle ahead. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive in traffic?

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go much faster or slower than other vehicles. Drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road must:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Assume other drivers will change lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is clear to do so.

questions.question: What can help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before braking.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas pedal first to slow down, then press the brake gently. This activates your brake lights and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

questions.question: A solid red HAWK (High Intensity Activated Crosswalk) signal means:

options.text: Drivers should slow down and prepare to stop.
Drivers must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: HAWK signals are used at pedestrian crossings. When the signal turns solid red, drivers must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Compared to driving during the day, driving at night is:
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see in the dark. Headlights from other cars can blind you. More tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are usually white with black markings and must always be obeyed.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow (or orange in work zones). They warn you of hazards ahead or areas where special rules apply.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: The start of a reduced speed zone.
The end of a reduced speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The end of a reduced speed zone.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the posted times. The "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights (if available) in fog. High beams bounce off the fog and reduce visibility even more.

questions.question: When in a travel lane on the roadway, you should:

options.text: Stop to look up an address.
Make a U-turn or back up if you miss an entrance ramp.
Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely leave the road. If you miss an exit, go to the next one. Do not back up or turn around on the freeway.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.

questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except when there is an emergency.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
The road turns sharply left, then sharply right.
The road curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means "Yield." Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and cross traffic go first. Stop only if necessary.

questions.question: You can pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs or other objects.
